chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Connect with your relatives, even if it is by a sip of water; and the best of what you can connect with the relatives is keeping harm away from them; and connecting with the relatives delays the death [time] and brings love among the family.

key_terms.مَنْسَأَةٌ فِي الْأَجَلِ: A delay in lifespan / Prolonging life

ai.seo_question: What is the best way to maintain good relations with relatives according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of *silat al-rahim* is expanded to include not just active connection but the passive virtue of withholding harm (*kaff al-adha*), which is considered the pinnacle of kinship. The hadith links this social duty to metaphysical benefits, asserting that maintaining ties extends one's lifespan (*mansa'ah fi al-ajal*) and strengthens emotional bonds (*mahabbah fi al-ahl*), a theme central to Shia ethical jurisprudence. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on family as the foundational unit of social stability and spiritual merit.
